newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn sees better chance for power consensus-report.
newsitem.headline: Bonn sees better chance for power consensus-report.

text.p: German Environment Minister Angela Merkel was quoted on Sunday as saying opposition Social Democrats might now be ready to compromise in a long stand-off which threatens to hold up the building of new nuclear plants.

In an advance release from its Monday edition, the daily Handelsblatt said SPD leaders including chairman Oskar Lafontaine had signalled they were ready to resume talks aimed at reaching a consensus on energy issues.

The SPD wants Germany to give up nuclear power, while Chancellor Helmut Kohl's coalition wants to maintain it. The SPD is also trying to maintain subsidies for the coal industry which the government is trying to curtail.

The electric power industry does not see a need for new reactors until about 2005, but long lead times are involved in building such plants and any utility would need to be sure that a future SPD-led government would not quash its plans.
Merkel was quoted as saying the need for talks was growing more urgent and that progress must be made in the area of nuclear waste disposal to ensure reactors remained in operation.
Gorleben, one proposed site for permanent waste storage, has been the scene of violent demonstrations against the shipments.
Merkel said the question of whether to continue using nuclear power could not be decided in a vacuum independent of international developments.
If Germany gave up its competence in nuclear technology, it can no longer play an active role in making reactors in the former Soviet sphere more secure, she said.
